title: Exact Candidate Certification
summary: Build one immutable Candidate, verify its executable payload in a static browser host, attach real visual, human and physical-device evidence to the same identity, then promote only certification metadata without changing payloadHash.
whenToUse: A playable Workspace is ready to produce an externally shared release candidate.
A Candidate must be promoted to Certified H5 without rebuilding or changing executable bytes.
Browser, VLM, human and device claims must refer to exactly the same artifact.
whenNotToUse: Early design exploration before a stable playable Candidate exists.
A workflow that allows fixture, synthetic, stale or emulated evidence to stand in for real release evidence.

inputs.description: A LoreWeaver Workspace compilable by the existing RuntimeSpec compiler.
specHash, runtimeVersion, payloadHash, artifact path and artifactSha256 from the selected Candidate.
Screenshot and screenshotSha256 captured from the same browser verification session.

stages.purpose: Compile the Workspace through the one Release Compiler and mark the artifact UNVERIFIED_CANDIDATE.
notes: Candidate export is shareable for testing but releaseEligible remains false.
The executable payload hash excludes certification metadata.

stages.purpose: Run the exact Candidate from a static host, enter every resolved node, verify Card and Modifier wiring, capture runtime errors and a final screenshot.
notes: The previous verified Browser anchor remains intact when a new attempt fails.
A newly selected Candidate invalidates package-bound downstream evidence.

stages.purpose: Review the exact browser screenshot with a real visual provider and bind the result to Candidate and screenshot identity.
notes: Only completed grok/codex real providers can produce release-eligible visual evidence.
Unavailable providers never degrade to a pass.

stages.purpose: Record a real player's completion, understanding, replay intent, clarity, difficulty, failures and suggestions against the same Candidate.
notes: fixture=false, synthetic=false and humanObserved=true are mandatory.
A failed playtest is recorded honestly and does not certify.

stages.purpose: Run the same Candidate on a real physical target device and record interaction, console and FPS observations against an explicit budget.
notes: physicalDevice=true, headless=false, emulated=false and synthetic=false are mandatory.

stages.purpose: Evaluate all used Gameplay Cards, evidence freshness, identity matching and waiver state before allowing promotion.
notes: The weakest used Card determines aggregate maturity.

stages.purpose: Promote the already verified Candidate by changing certification metadata only and proving payloadHash remains unchanged.
notes: The Candidate is promoted in place conceptually; the executable payload is not rebuilt.
The Certified artifact must preserve source Candidate payloadHash.

failureModes.description: An evidence report refers to another spec, payload, artifact or screenshot.
failureModes.requiredResponse: Block certification, select or rebuild the intended Candidate, and recollect all affected downstream evidence.

failureModes.description: Authoring, recipe, content, asset or runtime identity changed after evidence collection.
failureModes.requiredResponse: Mark old reports stale and rerun the affected verification stages.

failureModes.description: A new Candidate ZIP becomes the browser verification anchor.
failureModes.requiredResponse: Keep the new Browser report fresh while invalidating VLM, human, device and release state tied to the prior artifact.

failureModes.description: No supported real VLM provider completed the review.
failureModes.requiredResponse: Keep status unavailable and releaseEligible=false; do not substitute a fixture or synthetic pass.

failureModes.description: Certification metadata processing changed executable payload bytes.
failureModes.requiredResponse: Abort promotion and investigate the promoter/export boundary.

source.adaptation: Formalizes the already implemented exact-Candidate release chain using VibeGame's cross-role Contract pattern. No VibeGame implementation source is copied.
